result:
result: all six items done; build and verify exit 0. Item 1 was a real gap: specialist children did not see rpc mode, so the T3 gate did not hold for them.

Item 1 evidence: @tintinweb/pi-subagents 0.23.1 runs each specialist in-process and calls `session.bindExtensions({ onError })` with no `mode` (src/agent-runner.ts:1297). Pi's `_extensionMode` then defaults to "print" (pi-coding-agent dist/core/agent-session.js:165, 2742), so a child's `ctx.mode` is "print". The child does share `process.env`.
- Before the fix, `isT3Session` (needs rpc) was false in every child. A T3-hosted child would register browser-use, and `refuseT3PreviewOutsideT3` would refuse T3's preview tools.
- The fix is `hostedByT3(ctx, env, specialist)` in packages/integrations/pi/src/t3.ts. The root decides with `isT3Session` on every `session_start` and writes or deletes `HOLYAGENT_T3_HOSTED` in the shared env. The root also clears a stale value from outside. A specialist reads only that marker, never T3's own variables.
- It is used at extension.ts `t3: hostedByT3(ctx, env, isChild())`. `held.t3` feeds both `registerScreen` and `refuseT3PreviewOutsideT3`, so the two stay consistent.
- Two existing tests had simulated a child with mode rpc, which cannot happen. I changed them to start a root in rpc, then the child in print.

Other items:
- 2: `findChromium` and `chromiumFixFor` resolve a bare name through `findCommand` (Bun.which with the env's PATH key) via a new injectable `which` parameter. A name with `/` or `\` must still exist as given. It returns the resolved file. A missing path or name still gives the "does not exist" fix text.
- 3: Added `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, `XDG_DATA_HOME` and `UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR` to the allowlist; the allowlist test passes them through.
- 4: The timeout message now reads "did not answer within N ms: Chromium never wrote DevToolsActivePort in the profile directory <profile> or never answered on the port it reported (a Chromium wrapper that ignores --user-data-dir writes it elsewhere)".
- 5: On win32 `stopGroup` skips `killGroup`, and so `taskkill`, when `child.exitCode !== null`. Its `Pick` type now includes `exitCode`. The Unix path is unchanged.
- 6: docs/pi/screen.md says the allowlist is defense in depth only. It names the same-user risk: Python can read other processes' environments and the home directory. The allowlist sentence also lists the three new variables. I updated the T3 sentences in docs/pi/screen.md and docs/pi/t3-code.md to `hostedByT3` and the marker.

Tests added or changed:
- t3.test.ts: three `hostedByT3` cases.
- extension.test.ts: a specialist of a T3 root gets no browser-use and may use the preview tools; a specialist of a non-T3 root with T3 variables registers browser-use and is refused the preview tools.
- setup-chromium.test.ts: bare name via a fake `which`, separator paths never looked up on PATH, and one real PATH lookup in a temp folder.
- browser-launch.test.ts: allowlist, timeout message, win32 with exitCode 0 (no kill) and null (kill).
